title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The external device (EE2) transmits live GPS coordinates to the backend (P1). GPS coordinates are unique identifiers for the device's location. This linking through a unique identifier creates a threat where the backend can link the data to a specific individual.
assumptions: The GPS coordinates are unique identifiers for the device's location.

title: Observed Communications
description: The data flow involves the transmission of live GPS coordinates. This constitutes observed communications, where the data is transmitted and observed by the backend.
assumptions: The data is transmitted and observed by the backend.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The backend (P1) processes personal data (GPS coordinates) that is of a highly sensitive data type. This data is collected and processed more frequently than functionally needed, constituting a data disclosure threat.
assumptions: GPS coordinates are considered highly sensitive personal data.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend writes location pings to the Location History Store. This action links the data subject (identified by the app's unique identifier) to the data store using that identifier.
assumptions: The app uses a unique identifier to identify the user.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Location History Store stores location data. Location data is considered highly sensitive personal data and should only be collected and processed when strictly required.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Family Account Store (DS2) contains unique identifiers (e.g., user IDs, email addresses) that are used to link data to specific individuals. When the Geofencing Engine reads this data, it can identify the data subjects associated with the stored records, enabling the engine to link geofencing rules to specific individuals.
assumptions: The Family Account Store contains identifiable personal data.

title: Linking via Quasi-identifier
description: The data flow DF4 carries metadata about the parties involved in the data exchange (e.g., the specific user accounts being accessed). This metadata can be used to link the data flow to specific individuals, potentially enabling the Geofencing Engine to associate the flow with particular users.
assumptions: The data flow carries metadata about the parties involved.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) observes the data flow DF4 as it passes through. The act of reading and processing the data flow constitutes observed communications, which can be used to track the flow's movement and identify the data subjects involved.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine observes the data flow.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares an external identifier (e.g., email, ID number) with the mobile app backend (P1). This identifier is unique and can be used to link the parent's account to the child's profile, enabling the backend to identify the parent's identity.
assumptions: The identifier used by EE1 is globally unique or locally unique within the system.

title: Identifiable Information via Identifier
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares data that contains a unique reference to its identity (e.g., a unique ID). This data is processed by the backend (P1), allowing the backend to identify the parent's identity.
assumptions: The identifier in EE1's data is unique to the parent.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares personal data (name, DOB, school) with the backend (P1). This data is of a highly sensitive type (PII) and is processed by a system that may not be designed to handle such data, leading to potential privacy risks.
assumptions: The data type is sensitive and requires strict handling.

title: Data Type Granularity
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares personal data with the backend (P1). The data is of a fine-grained level (e.g., specific DOB, school) which may be more granular than functionally required for the child's profile creation.
assumptions: The data granularity is finer than necessary for the specific use case.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares personal data (name, DOB, school) with the backend (P1) for the purpose of creating a child's profile. This processing is not strictly necessary to achieve the functional goal of the parent's account creation.
assumptions: The data is shared for a purpose that does not require this level of detail.

title: Involved Parties
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares personal data with the backend (P1). The backend may be a dynamic set of parties (e.g., multiple data processors, cloud services) that are not known or targeted at the initial design, amplifying the exposure risk.
assumptions: The backend is a dynamic set of parties, not a static, targeted one.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The parent entity (EE1) may not be aware that its personal data (name, DOB, school) is being processed by the backend (P1) for profile creation, leading to a lack of control over how the data is used.
assumptions: The parent is unaware of the specific processing activity.

title: Lawful Processing
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares personal data with the backend (P1) without valid consent or a lawful basis, potentially violating privacy regulations.
assumptions: The processing lacks a valid legal ground (e.g., consent, legal obligation).

title: Storage Limitation
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares personal data with the backend (P1) for a purpose that may not require long-term storage, but the data is kept longer than functionally needed.
assumptions: The data is stored longer than necessary for the child's profile.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier

If these data elements contain unique identifiers (e.g., user IDs, email addresses, or geofence zone codes) that are globally or locally unique, the sharing of this data enables the Family Account & Permissions Store to link or identify the data subjects. This constitutes a genuine threat of Linking (L) at the source element.
assumptions: The data elements shared by P1 (account, child profile, geofence zone) contain unique identifiers.

title: Identifying via Identifier
description: The backend process shares account, child profile, and geofence zone data with the Family Account & Permissions Store. If these data elements contain unique identifiers (e.g., user IDs, email addresses, or geofence zone codes) that are unique to the data subject, the sharing of this data enables the Family Account & Permissions Store to identify the data subject. This constitutes a genuine threat of Identifying (I) at the source element.
assumptions: The data elements shared by P1 (account, child profile, geofence zone) contain unique identifiers.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The backend process shares account, child profile, and geofence zone data with the Family Account & Permissions Store. If the data elements shared are highly sensitive (e.g., personal identifiers, biometric data, or location data), the sharing of this data may be perceived as excessive. This constitutes a genuine threat of Data Disclosure (Dd) at the source element.

title: Lawful Processing Concerns
description: The backend process shares account, child profile, and geofence zone data with the Family Account & Permissions Store. If the processing of this data is not lawful (e.g., lacks valid consent or is based on incorrect lawful grounds), the sharing of this data may lead to non-compliance with regulations. This constitutes a genuine threat of Non-compliance (Nc) at the source element.
assumptions: The processing of the data elements shared by P1 (account, child profile, geofence zone) is not lawful.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier

This linking through quasi-identifiers creates a privacy risk as the data subject's identity can be inferred from the data flow.

title: Observed Communications
description: The data flow involves retrieving location history, which is observed communications.
